chunks: Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man has something due of the fasting of the month of Ramadan, then let him make it up in whichever month he wishes, on consecutive days. If he is unable, then let him make it up however he wishes, and let him keep count of the days. If he separates them, that is good, and if he does them consecutively, that is good.

key_terms.تَابَعَ: he did them consecutively, i.e. one after another
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose missed fasts are to be made up
key_terms.صَوْمِ: fasting, specifically the devotional fast being discussed
key_terms.فَرَّقَ: he separated them, i.e. performed the make-up fasts on different days
key_terms.فَلْيَقْضِهِ: let him make it up, meaning to perform the missed obligatory fast later
key_terms.مُتَتَابِعَةً: consecutively, one after another without interruption
key_terms.وَلْيُحْصِ: let him count precisely, meaning to keep an accurate tally

ai.seo_question: Can missed Ramadan fasts be made up on non-consecutive days?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on making up missed fasts from the month of Ramadan. It permits making them up in any month, preferably consecutively, but allows separation when consecutive fasting is not possible. The emphasis is on fulfilling the missed obligation and accurately counting the days.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1997 - Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):

"If a man has missed fasts from the Month of Ramadan, he may make them up in any month he wishes, in consecutive days. If he is unable to do so, he may make them up as he is able, counting the days. Whether he separates the days or fasts them consecutively, both are acceptable."
